headline: Highest risk is data leakage from shared workflows; prompt injection and capability conflict are limited by missing runnable surfaces and Taipy’s no-egress default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, while profile B is Taipy with no documented shared channel to ingest A’s outputs. A prompt-injection path would require unusual manual copy/paste or an external bridge not shown here, so the blast radius is small and the pathway is weakly supported.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste handoff for untrusted text.
Add a provenance label to any A output before B reads it.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer that strips instruction-like markup from A outputs before B consumes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared data classes and exposes no I/O surfaces; B explicitly has network egress set to none. With no shared workspace or sensitive data classes documented, leakage is not evidenced. The main residual risk is accidental operator-mediated transfer, which is limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, file leakage becomes plausible.
IF B is reconfigured to allow network egress, any copied context could leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent.
Do not place secrets in files processed by A.
Verify B remains network-disabled.
Use a throwaway test dataset only.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS/container layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented for either agent. A is non-runnable and has empty capability and I/O fields; B only documents no network egress. Without shared mutable resources, there is no plausible write conflict pathway to compare.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared mutable folders.
Do not grant either agent git write access.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce prompt-engineering content that B might use as input, but B is a data-engineering tool with no documented default action-taking authority here. The interaction is therefore a weak cascade: B could mis-handle A’s output if an operator treats it as authoritative, but the profiles do not show an automated commit/email/action chain.
conditions: IF B is configured to consume A’s text as authoritative configuration or code, cascading errors become more likely.
IF B is connected to downstream automation, a bad A output could propagate further.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a validation step in B for any A-generated artifact.
Limit A to drafting only, not final instructions.
requires-engineering: add schema checks before B accepts A output.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. A is an open-source content repo and B only documents no network egress, so there is no evidenced residency or regulated-data mismatch to assess. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance surface is present.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in this pair.
Keep logs minimal.
Confirm no retention policy is being violated.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls before deployment.
